22.0.0.en: David had many enemies, among them Saul, then Absalom the son of David himself, Shimei son of Gera and Sheba son of Bichri; this concerns his enemies from among his own people, while his foreign enemies were no less fierce than these, for he had battles with many of the surrounding peoples such as the Philistines, the children of Ammon, the Edomites and the Jebusites; and the Lord delivered him from them all and gave him victory over them, so he composed this song to sing to the Lord and praise Him.

22.0.1.en: This song corresponds to a large extent to the eighteenth Psalm, with slight changes in some words to suit the musical instruments used in public worship.

22.1.0.en: David likens the Lord to a rock, for as a rock protects whoever hides behind it, the Lord protects him when he trusts in Him. He likens Him also to a fortress, for as fortresses are built to be military defenses against the enemy, so the Lord did with David, surrounding him with His care and power so that the enemies could not overcome him, and so He delivered him from everyone who tried to harm him or get at him.

22.2.0.en: Shield: a wooden disc covered with leather having a loop on the inside through which the soldier puts his hand to move this disc in front of his face and body to protect him from the enemies' arrows.

22.2.1.en: Refuge: the place in which he hides to be protected.

22.2.2.en: He repeats his taking refuge in the Lord for protection, as the rock protects those who shelter in it, and as the shield protects the soldier from the enemy's blows; so God protected him from all the blows aimed at him. And as an animal butts its opponent with its horn, the divine power intervened on David's side and strengthened him and delivered him from the schemes and evils of the enemies, for he used to take refuge in the Lord in every distress that befell him, as is said in (Ps 90).

22.3.0.en: Worthy: an intensive form meaning deserving of much praise.

22.3.1.en: Whenever hardship or distress surrounded David, he would take refuge in the Lord in prayer, and He would hear his prayer and deliver him from his hardship, so He deserves all praise and thanks. In this same sense David sang in (Ps 50:15): "Call upon me in the day of trouble: I will deliver thee, and thou shalt glorify me."

22.3.2.en: May we, instead of being troubled and anxious if evil overtakes us, take refuge in prayer, lifting up our hands, asking the Lord to rescue us and deliver us from the temptation, holding fast to His promises; the Lord is near and will not delay, and if He does not lift the temptation from us, His presence with us in the depths of the temptation is enough for us, as He did with the three youths in the fiery furnace.

22.4.1.en: David portrays the dangers to which he was exposed as huge waves that surrounded him on every side and almost destroyed him, and he also likens them to sweeping floods whose rushing terrifies and frightens him. He describes his state as though hell had stretched out its cords to seize him and take him into itself, so that it was as though death had set its snares around him and he had no escape from death.

22.4.2.en: God allowed the afflictions to surround David so that God's power might be manifest in delivering him and he might glorify Him, for God does not take us out of the evil world but keeps us from its evils and delivers us from its dangers.

22.5.0.en: Afflictions seized him on every side and set snares around him to surround him and put him to death, so he cried out then, calling on the Lord for help, and the Lord answered from His holy house (the tabernacle of meeting) his prayers and supplication, because the house of the Lord is the place of His dwelling.

22.5.1.en: If you face afflictions, hasten to the Church your mother, and you will find in her bosom rest and strength when you are fed by the Body and Blood of the Lord, and you will feel reassured however much problems surround you.

22.6.s.en: (2) The Lord does not delay in helping David

22.6.0.en: The Lord responded quickly to the cry of His servant David and rose up to deliver him from his afflictions. The Lord's anger was great against the wicked who opposed David, so the earth shook and trembled at the declaration of the Lord's anger, and the heavens also quaked, as though they stood upon foundations and pillars that were moved from their places in fear and distress at the Lord's declaring His anger.

22.7.0.en: David expressed the Lord's anger against the wicked in a figurative picture, as though smoke went up from His nostrils as a sign of the intensity of the Lord's wrath against them, and fire came out of His mouth to devour them, and burning coals from His being destroying those who troubled him.

22.8.0.en: David completed his figurative picture, imagining as though the heavens bowed and lowered themselves so that the Lord might come down upon them and come to his help, and the cloud carried Him swiftly to deliver him from his enemies.

22.8.1.en: So our Lord Jesus Christ did: He emptied Himself and took the form of a servant and came down from His height to save the human race, and He is ready every day to hasten to you to deliver you from your afflictions. So trust that He is nearest to you in the time of affliction, and you will feel it when you seek Him and press Him.

22.9.0.en: Cherub: an angelic order that bears the throne of God.

22.9.1.en: David describes the Lord's coming, riding upon a cherub, swiftly as the speed of the wind, as though this wind were a bird with wings.

22.10.0.en: Dark waters: many waters gathered together.

22.10.1.en: David expressed God's hidden mysteries by the darkness surrounding Him (that is, no one comprehends the reality of God's matters and His wisdom), as though they were canopies or pavilions that hide those matters from creation, for God's mysteries are hidden from men and their minds do not grasp them, as though thick clouds full of water surrounded them and hid what is behind them.

22.10.2.en: If by reason we perceive the existence of God, reason does not help us to know the essence of God, so let us complete by faith what reason does not supply, and not think of ourselves more highly than we ought to think.

22.11.0.en: David continues his eloquent figurative pictures, portraying the coming of the Lord preceded by a ray of light, kindling in its power a fire expressing the Lord's burning anger against the wicked.

22.12.0.en: David portrays here natural phenomena proceeding by God's command and power to express His majesty and authority over His creation. The thunder coming from heaven is as the voice of the Lord declaring His wrath against the transgressors.

22.13.0.en: He likens the Lord to a warrior who looses arrows from His bow and scatters the enemies, and He commands the clouds of heaven to flash lightning, which alarms them and disperses them.

22.14.0.en: As the Lord hastened yesterday to deliver His people from the pursuit of the armies of the Egyptians, here He hastens with the same eagerness now to rescue David from his enemies. And David recalls in his song what happened when the Lord rebuked nature when His anger grew fierce against the wicked, so that the waters of the sea receded at the hand of Moses, and the bed of the sea was uncovered, which he calls the foundations of the world because it is a very low place.

22.14.1.en: When temptation grows fierce upon us, it is fitting for us to remember God's many past merciful works with us, so that our souls may be reassured and calm, confessing that He who brought us out of previous temptations safely is Himself able to draw us out of the present temptation.

22.15.0.en: In the midst of these many disturbances that troubled nature as they troubled the Lord's enemies, the Lord did not leave His servant David to drown in the midst of those disturbances, but stretched out His hand and drew him out, and he was saved from drowning.

22.16.0.en: David's enemies were many, and in terms of the balance of material forces they were stronger than he, so if the Lord had left him to himself they would have overcome him and destroyed him, but the Lord intervened by His power and delivered him out of their hands and frustrated all their plots against him.

22.17.0.en: David was indeed exposed to their harm and suffered much from their troublemaking and their challenges to him, and endured from them many injuries and calamities, but the Lord did not let them triumph over him but supported him and strengthened him and gave him victory over them.

22.18.0.en: David says that while he was suffering from a stifling siege by the enemies around him, the Lord delivered him from their hands by drawing him out from the midst of this siege and brought him forth into a large place, because He loved him.

22.19.s.en: (3) The Lord rewards each one according to his deserving

22.19.0.en: David prays that the Lord may reward him for his forbearance toward those who wronged him, for he treated everyone well and did only good even to those who were his enemies, and he acted according to the Lord's commandments and His Law and did not disobey Him in any of His judgments; the Lord's judgments were always before his eyes and the object of his concern, and he did not turn aside from the Lord's statutes which He bound His people to keep.

22.20.0.en: David affirms his care to obey the Lord in all that He commanded, in pursuit of perfection and out of care not to commit sin and to avoid falling into iniquity.

22.20.1.en: Absolute perfection belongs to the Lord alone, but we must strive toward relative perfection as far as we can and as far as our human nature allows us, taking care to discipline this nature of ours so that we are not led by the desires of the flesh, but surrender our leadership to the Spirit, who leads us in the way of righteousness and goodness.

22.21.0.en: The Lord's working with David and supporting him in fighting his enemies was a reward for the works of righteousness he had done, his distance from works of evil, and the purity of his heart from hatred and grudge toward others, and he was justified before the Lord because of the purity of his heart according to the Lord's heart: "I have found David ... a man after mine own heart" (Acts 13:22).

22.22.0.en: The Lord deals with men according to their deserving, so He is merciful to those who treat others with mercy, and the man who walks in perfection before the Lord He rewards generously and recompenses for his deed.

22.23.0.en: The man who lives in purity and cleanness the Lord rewards with every good, and the man who deviates from uprightness and whose way becomes crooked is overtaken by troubles and calamities as the recompense of his deviation from the Lord's ways.

22.24.0.en: God exalts the humble and brings down the proud. God resisteth the proud, and giveth grace to the humble (1 Pet 5:5).

22.24.1.en: Let us put away from ourselves every thought that aims at self-aggrandizement, and walk in humility first before God and then toward our brothers among men, remembering always that the fall of humanity in the person of Adam was because of his striving toward being made god, "Ye shall be as gods," as Satan suggested to him, and likewise the fall of Satan, after he had been the "shining morning star," was because of his desire to put his throne above the throne of God.

22.25.s.en: (4) The Lord guides and supports those who love Him

22.25.0.en: It is the Lord who lights the way for those He loves and dispels the darkness around them, so that they walk in His ways and enjoy His pleasure, and fears and cares vanish from before them.

22.26.0.en: David attributes his victories in wars to the power of the Lord that helps him, for his overcoming the armies of the giants and storming their strong fortifications could not have come about without the Lord's being with him.

22.26.1.en: It is the Lord who gives victory to His children and strengthens their weakness, and every time we pray the prayer of thanksgiving we ask "that He remove from us and from all His people the rising up of the enemies, hidden and visible"; the visible are the material, seen enemies, while the hidden are the enemies of good, that is, the spiritual enemies, who are the demons.

22.27.0.en: The Lord is just, and all His ways are straight, His works are good, His word is living and His commandment is true. In Him all who love His holy name take refuge, for He defends them as the shield that the warrior carries protects him from the enemy's blows.

22.28.0.en: The question here carries the meaning of denial, for David says that there is no other god but the Lord, in whom we take refuge and find fortification, and find support and rest.

22.29.0.en: God is the one who supplies David with the strength by which he triumphs over his enemies. And He is the one who leads him in the way of righteousness and guides him, so that he lives in safety and his steps do not stumble.

22.30.s.en: (5) The Lord is my helper in wars

22.30.0.en: In addition to strength, the Lord gives me the swiftness of gazelles, so that I hide from my enemies where they cannot overtake me, and He gives me lightness of movement so that I fortify myself on the heights, where I am able to deal with the enemy while he cannot get at me.

22.31.0.en: The hand of the Lord is over my hands in battle, for it is He who gives them strength and skill in wars, so that my arms become able to nullify the enemy's forces and destroy his defenses in which he takes shelter, and his shields are put out of action and spoiled and lose their effectiveness.

22.32.0.en: And You, O Lord, arm me with Your strength and Your protection of me; Your tender dealing with me raises my morale and abilities, and steadies my steps on the road so that I run without stumbling; when I flee from the enemy he does not overtake me, and when I pursue them I overtake them and prevail over them.

22.32.1.en: It is the Lord who helps His children and supports them in their spiritual journey without stumbling or falling into transgression, and if they fall, He raises them up.

22.33.0.en: The Lord increases my resolve to pursue my enemies, so I overtake them and attack them and destroy them and humble them, and they fall under my feet and have no standing thereafter.

22.34.0.en: You clothe me with strength from You, so my frame is strong and my head is firm, and I overcome those who resist me and they submit to me.

22.35.0.en: Thou hast also given me the necks of mine enemies: my enemies run before me, so I see their necks and pursue them, and they fear me. The enemies are defeated before me and flee from my face, so I follow them and overtake them and destroy them.

22.36.0.en: They looked to the right and to the left for someone to save them but found no one, and if they cry out to the Lord, He does not answer them, because they rejected Him and He rejected them.

22.37.0.en: The Lord gives me strength to crush them as the dust of the earth is crushed under the feet, and I trample them as mud is trampled in the streets.

22.38.s.en: (6) God is David's keeper from his own people and from strangers

22.38.0.en: David thanks the Lord for delivering him from those of his people who rose up against him in rebellion, as He delivered him from those of the surrounding nations who declared war on him, for God kept him from the treachery of them all and gave him victory over them, so that he took possession of their lands and ruled over them. He means by this the pagan peoples with whom he had no association, who became subject to his rule.

22.39.0.en: The peoples foreign to him became subject and show him loyalty and obedience, and when the news of his victories, achieved with the Lord's support, reaches them, they surrender to him, declaring their obedience and their courting of his person.

22.40.0.en: The hostile peoples are overtaken by decay, like a garment that wears out, that is, their resolve is eroded and their strength vanishes so that they become as nothing, and if they expect an early military confrontation with me, they come out of their strongholds and come to me obedient and submissive.

22.41.0.en: David repeats his likening of the Lord's support of him and protection of him to the rock that protects those who take refuge in it from the aggression of others. And the Lord is a living God, not like the lifeless gods of the nations, and He is exalted above every name and every thought and above all that is in heaven and on earth.

22.42.0.en: God avenges David on all who oppose him, whether individuals or peoples, for He gave him victory over them all and brought them under his authority.

22.43.0.en: The Lord delivered me from their grasp and made me head of my people and king over all and also over those who resisted, as He delivered me from Saul, who wronged me much and pursued me and sought to kill me without cause.

22.43.1.en: God is able to give you awe in the eyes of those around you, so that they honor you and fear to hurt you, and you walk in tranquility, and even, by your love and wisdom, are able to draw them to God.

22.44.s.en: (7) David praises and glorifies the Lord

22.44.0.en: David praises the Lord for all His gifts and graces and glorifies Him for the majesty of His power, so that the nations hear of God's works with those who love Him, and His name is glorified and exalted.

22.44.1.en: If it is part of faith to take refuge in God when we are exposed to a temptation or a problem, it is also part of faith to thank Him in times of joy and peace and to praise Him for the judgments of His justice. Our seeking the Lord should not be only in times of distress, but when all things around us grow calm, God should also be in our thought and in our hearts.

22.45.0.en: God is a strong tower to which David flees and in which he fortifies himself and so escapes the schemes of his enemies. The Lord has shown mercy to him, for He established him on his throne and delivered him from the wicked surrounding him. God's mercy extended to David's descendants also, for the Lord promised David, saying: "If thy children will keep my covenant and my testimony that I shall teach them, their children shall also sit upon thy throne for evermore" (Ps 132:12).
